title: Zephyrine and the Debt
premise: Sable Vane, a burned-out interpreter for a collapsing peace delegation, receives a calendar invite from his handler, Elias Mott—sent two days after Mott's body was pulled from the harbor. The invitation leads him to a dead-drop containing proof that the 'incident' that broke his sleep was no accident but a sanctioned operation to sabotage the treaty, implicating officials in all three governments. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Ferrow and betrayed by the delegation's own chairwoman, Sable assembles a ragtag found family of exiles and clerks who help him smuggle the evidence into the final summit session. In the end he reads the truth aloud in three languages before the cameras, trading his invisibility for exile—but gaining, for the first time, a family worth belonging to.
about_author: Oscar Almeida is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade behind glass booths in cities where treaties were signed and quietly broken. He writes thrillers about the people who translate violence and are never meant to be seen.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Insomniac and half-invisible within the failing peace delegation, Sable receives a meeting request from Elias Mott—his handler, dead forty-eight hours. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into compulsion: grief curdling into the first curiosity he's allowed himself since the incident. He goes to the dead-drop instead of reporting it.

chapters.title: What Mott Left Behind
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In a harbor locker he finds a drive: intercepted orders proving the incident—a convoy strike the delegation blamed on insurgents—was authorized from inside all three governments. The beat is vertigo; the safe numbness of his guilt dissolves when he realizes he witnessed a murder, not a tragedy. Ferrow watches him leave the locker.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ferrow. Sable tests the evidence against his own memory of interpreting the convoy radio traffic, confirming its authenticity. Ferrow reports to an unnamed principal and requests permission to handle Sable 'quietly.' The beat is cold dread on both sides of the hunt—the hunter revealed as another instrument, not a monster.

chapters.title: The Chairwoman's Smile
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable brings fragments to Chairwoman Ilse Renn, hoping the delegation itself can act; her warm reassurance convinces him—until he notices she already knew the date of the incident. The beat is betrayal and self-blame: he has handed the hunters his last map. He flees the delegation compound at night.

chapters.title: People Who Don't Sleep Either
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Hiding in a laundromat basement, Sable falls in with the delegation's discarded staff: a dismissed stenographer, a defected driver, a cook with three passports. They each recognize pieces of the conspiracy. The beat is warmth breaking through fear—the found family forms around shared sleeplessness and shared disposability.

chapters.title: Ferrow's Terms
chapters.summary: Ferrow's POV. Ferrow corners Sable alone and offers a trade: the drive for his life and silence. Sable counters by asking what Ferrow was promised—and learns Ferrow's own sister died in the convoy strike. The beat is uneasy recognition; enemy and interpreter see themselves in each other. No deal is struck, but something cracks open.

chapters.title: The Stenographer's Key
chapters.summary: Stenographer Mara's POV. Mara decrypts the drive fully using archived shorthand she was fired for keeping, revealing the operation's author: the delegation's own security director, with Renn's signature buried in a cipher. The beat is triumph turning to terror—they now hold the truth, and the summit ends in four days, after which the evidence dies with the treaty.

chapters.title: Everything We Carried
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Preparing to breach the summit, the group plans three simultaneous routes—one per government checkpoint—each member volunteering for the most dangerous leg. Ferrow, off-leash after refusing a second order, sends Sable an anonymous warning of the security sweep. The beat is chosen sacrifice: invisible people deciding to be seen together.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inside the closing session, Sable seizes the floor during interpretation and reads the evidence aloud in all three official languages while Mara broadcasts the drive. Guards close in; Renn denounces him live. The climax beat is ferocious clarity—every word he has ever translated was someone else's; these are finally his own.

chapters.title: A Family Worth Exile
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, coda. Stripped of credentials and facing charges in three countries, Sable waits in detention—until Ferrow walks in as his court-appointed 'translator,' and the others arrive as witnesses. The truth has forced inquiries in two governments. The beat is quiet belonging: he still doesn't sleep through the night, but now he isn't alone when he wakes.
